items.title: A scaled Chebyshev polynomial suppresses a separated interval
items.statement:
Let $a>b>c$ be real numbers, let $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\ge0$, and put

$$\xi(x):=\frac{2x-b-c}{b-c},\qquad \xi_a:=\xi(a)=1+\frac{2(a-b)}{b-c}>1.$$

Define

$$p_k(x):=\frac{T_k(\xi(x))}{T_k(\xi_a)},$$

where $T_k$ is the $k$th Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind from
[[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]]. Then $p_k$ is a real
polynomial of degree exactly $k$, $p_k(a)=1$, and

$$\max_{x\in[c,b]}|p_k(x)|=\frac{1}{T_k(\xi_a)}.$$

items.title: Two-pass MGS Arnoldi has an explicit local relation and an a posteriori orthogonality bound
items.statement: In the stated operationwise floating-point model, prove a local Arnoldi relation with explicit matvec, projection, normalization, and reorthogonalization error terms, then quantify the computed basis orthogonality loss under a full-rank/conditioning hypothesis and give a distinct breakdown or inconclusive branch.

items.title: Finite-precision CG has a recursive-residual gap and an attainable-accuracy bound
items.statement: For the stated rounded CG updates on an SPD system, prove a cumulative bound between the recursively updated residual and b−Ax, and convert a recomputed true-residual bound to an A-norm error bound without claiming exact-grade termination or monotonicity of the true residual.

items.title: Lanczos largest Ritz values obey a Chebyshev start-angle bound, including degenerate branches
items.statement: Prove the extremal Ritz-value bound for a real symmetric matrix with a separated top eigenspace, retaining the start-angle factor and spectral gap; treat a collapsed unwanted interval, zero top component, repeated top eigenvalue, dimension-one case, and exact invariant-subspace breakdown separately. Exact top recovery in the collapsed unwanted interval requires a nonzero top-eigenspace start component.

items.title: A computed GMRES correction has an explicit finite-precision residual gap
items.statement: From the local finite-precision Arnoldi relation, prove an explicit gap bound for a computed GMRES coefficient vector and a recomputed true residual; retain the basis-orthogonality and least-squares residual terms separately.

items.title: Unrestarted GMRES has a sparse matvec plus orthogonalization work bound
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ have a canonical CSR representation, with
$n\ge1$, at least one stored entry in every row, and
$s=\operatorname{nnz}(A)$. Let $r_0=b-Ax_0\ne0$ and $1\le m\le n$. Run
unrestarted GMRES in exact arithmetic for at most $m$ Arnoldi columns. At
column $j$, compute one CSR matrix-vector product, orthogonalize against the
$j$ existing vectors by either one or two complete modified Gram–Schmidt
passes, and update the projected least-squares problem by applying prior
Givens rotations and forming one new rotation. Each Givens rotation is an
orthogonal $2\times2$ matrix on adjacent rows chosen to zero the current
subdiagonal entry. If Arnoldi completes $m$
columns without breakdown, solve the resulting upper-triangular least-squares
factor; if it breaks down earlier, stop at that column and make no claim about
a separate rank-deficient fallback solve. Count field arithmetic and index
work, and exclude the stored input matrix. The total work in the no-breakdown
branch is $O(ms+m^2n)$ and the Krylov working storage is $O(mn)$. The same
bounds cover all matvec, orthogonalization, and projected-rotation work
actually performed before an earlier breakdown. These are operation and
storage bounds, not convergence or runtime claims.

title: Krylov methods and Lanczos convergence — Examples

items.title: Unrestarted GMRES solves a two-dimensional diagonal system before GMRES(1) restarts
items.statement: Verify the two-step unrestarted and one-step restarted behavior for A=diag(1,2), b=(1,1), x0=0, including the nonzero first-cycle restarted residual.

items.title: CG's positive-denominator hypothesis fails on an indefinite system while MINRES can start
items.statement: Compute the zero first CG denominator for diag(1,−1), verify that the first MINRES least-squares problem is defined and that the exact solution lies in K₂, then contrast with an SPD CG denominator.

items.title: A poorly aligned start delays the largest Ritz value and requires the start-angle factor
items.statement: For A=diag(10,2,1) and b=(1/100,√(9999/20000),√(9999/20000)), verify the unit start, prove θ₂<9/4, and show deleting the start-angle factor makes the stated Chebyshev bound false.

items.title: Lanczos handles repeated top eigenvalues, absent top components, and exact breakdown
items.statement: Check the scalar-matrix branch, a repeated top eigenvalue with collapsed unwanted interval, a start vector with zero top projection, and a top-containing invariant-subspace breakdown.
